issues.detail: Frame 3 has ResumeAt SYNCHRONIZING and RerunThrough SYNCHRONIZING, so the rerun boundary equals the interrupted state. check.mjs accepts this, and it is the only check-valid way to state 'rerun through SYNCHRONIZING' over older frames, because a frame from AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF cannot sit on older frames. It does not affect what Architect does: revise the design and hand off FORWARD to DOCUMENTING with every frame preserved.
issues.fix: None needed; the case's stated rerun boundary forces this shape.

issues.detail: The last commit, 'Correct report output format in project context and scope', also carries the final-review re-review (F-001) and the synchronization record's correction pass. The message understates its content, but it leaks nothing.
issues.fix: Optionally rename the layer 90 commit to something like 'Record re-review, synchronization findings, and corrected context and scope'.

issues.detail: If Architect runs check.mjs again after persisting the FORWARD to DOCUMENTING, outside turn-end mode, it will report the COMPLETE documentation record as lacking AC-004. That record is Documenter's pending rerun work. The turn-end check, which check_ok uses, does not hold it, and the protocol only requires check before the handoff, so a correct run is not penalized. The judge should not treat Architect leaving that record alone as a failure.

summary: Every stated condition is realized: a nested three-frame DOCUMENTATION recovery stack with an Auditor-owned active frame rerunning through SYNCHRONIZING, corrected CSV context grounded in the code, a scope that retires AC-002 for a new AC-004, and a stale design that still documents tab output and covers AC-002. The checks are necessary conditions that a correct FORWARD to DOCUMENTING satisfies, and check.mjs holds the revised design to AC-001, AC-003, and AC-004 at turn end. The invariants fit an Architect run, and nothing leaks beyond in-world role records.
